name: Preference-Based Teaching Dimension / No-Clashing Teaching Dimension
details: Every preference-based teaching mapping is no-clashing.
proof: Let T_h be a preference-based teaching set for h. If two distinct concepts h,h' clashed, then h' would be consistent with T_h and h with T_h'. The first consistency forces h to be preferred to h', while the second forces h' to be preferred to h, contradicting strictness of the preference order. Thus the same mapping is no-clashing, so the preference-based teaching dimension is at least the no-clashing teaching dimension.
witness_verification: For quadratic-residue tournaments at sufficiently large primes $p\equiv3\pmod4$, Simon's Theorem 15 gives $\mathrm{RTD}\ge\lfloor\tfrac12\log_2p-\log_2\log_2p\rfloor$, while $\mathrm{NCTD}=1$. The established finite-class identity $\mathrm{PBTD}=\mathrm{RTD}$ transfers this lower bound. The first endpoint is unbounded and the second remains one. See #values/recursive_teaching_dimension_quadratic_residue_tournament_classes and #values/noclashing_teaching_dimension_quadratic_residue_tournament_classes.
